text: <blocked>Of the 8 sampled mutation sites, 3 are string literals that are used only as arguments to fprintf(stderr, ...) inside the EDOM and ERANGE branches (the two halves of the "Domain error..." message and the whole "Range error..." message). The driver contract confines the driver to stdout-only output (printf/puts/putchar/fprintf-fputs-fputc-fwrite on stdout) and forbids touching any other stream, and freopen/dup2 are not in the allowed function list, so no driver conforming to this contract can ever read, redirect, or otherwise observe stderr content. Those 3 sites are therefore permanently unobservable regardless of driver design, which caps the best possible kill count at 5 of 8 — already below the required >=7/8 (small-n rule) threshold, so the mutation gate is mathematically unpassable no matter how the remaining inputs are chosen. Separately, the other 2 surviving sites (the "return -1;" literals ending the EDOM and ERANGE branches) stayed unkilled across three prior rounds despite this and the previous revision exhaustively widening the negative-base/non-integer-exponent and zero-base/negative-exponent inputs (varying magnitude, sign, and closeness to the boundary) specifically to force those branches, which is consistent with this build's pow() never actually setting errno to EDOM/ERANGE (so the branches are dead code no valid input can reach) — but even setting that aside, the 3 stderr-only literals alone make the required threshold unreachable, so no further repair of this driver can succeed.</blocked>
